# orchestration_reopen_tool

> Reopen a workflow execution that FAILED or was CANCELLED, so it can pick up where it left off instead of being abandoned.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | `orchestration` |
| Callable | MCP clients; in-app @ai conversations; grantable to agents |
| Filter | `https://www.dsiloed.com/api/v1/mcp?tools=orchestration_reopen_tool` |

## Description

This is the description the server sends to the model, verbatim.

Reopen a workflow execution that FAILED or was CANCELLED, so it can pick up
where it left off instead of being abandoned.

Use this when a run died on something fixable — a gate that was wrong, a
worker that could not satisfy a check, an environment problem since resolved —
and its completed work (branches, artifacts, requirement tasks) is still good.
Starting a fresh run would throw that away; reopening keeps the whole lineage.

A failed run is otherwise a dead end: every retry path refuses once the run is
marked completed, so without this the only option is a brand-new execution.

This clears the terminal state and returns the run to `orch_running`, then (by
default) retries the stage that failed so work resumes immediately. Pass
retry_stage: false to reopen without re-running anything — useful when you want
to fix data or approve a gate first.

FIX THE CAUSE FIRST. Reopening a run whose underlying failure is still present
just burns another attempt on the same wall. `reason` is required and is
recorded permanently on the run (who reopened it and why).

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `orchestration_execution_id` | integer | yes | The failed/cancelled workflow execution to reopen. |
| `reason` | string | yes | REQUIRED. Why this run is being reopened, and what changed so it can now succeed (e.g. "cross-repo test gate fixed in !1076 — dev children no longer asked for other repos' results"). Stored permanently on the run as audit. |
| `stage_execution_id` | integer | no | Optional. The specific stage to resume from. Defaults to the run's current stage. |
| `retry_stage` | boolean | no | Whether to immediately retry the stage after reopening (default true). Set false to reopen the run without launching any work yet. |
